subject: Brightlane POC — Observability action plan and evaluation checklist
messages:
From: Sanjay Patel <sanjay.p@brightlane.health>
To: rafael.mendes@redwood.ai, marissa.cole@redwood.ai, laura.bennett@redwood.ai
Cc: claire@brightlane.health
Date: Thu, 18 Mar 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Brightlane / Redwood — post-call summary + target success criteria

Thanks team — good sync earlier. Quick recap from our side and what we need for the POC so we can align procurement/ops.

1) High-level objective
- Validate Redwood’s ability to serve clinical-quality summarization and routing at our expected scale for a single clinical product pipeline. Focus: latency, reliability, and observability so our QA and compliance teams can validate behavior.

2) Core success criteria (what our stakeholders care about)
- Latency: p95 end-to-end inference latency for our standard 256-token prompt <= 400ms for interactive flows (target), p95 <= 800ms acceptable under load.
- Reliability: >= 99% successful responses (no server errors) during a defined 72-hour run at our target concurrency.
- Throughput: sustain 150 concurrent requests with <5% request queueing for sustained 30-minute runs.
- Cost signal: token-level cost reporting so we can estimate $/1000 tokens during the trial.
- Functional: model outputs meet our QA pass rate on the provided prompt set (we will send the test set).

3) Observability needs
- Dashboards for latency (p50/p95/p99), request rate, error rates by error code, model version, and route.
- Trace sampling for end-to-end request traces that include: request_id, user_id, model_variant, kernel fallback events.
- Logs: structured JSON logs exported to our S3 bucket for retention and audit (14-day retention initially).
- Metrics: token counts per request, KV cache hit ratio, queue depth, batch size distribution.

4) Next steps we need from Redwood
- POC plan + timeline, owners (integration / observability / infra), and an onboarding checklist for access (IP allowlist, service accounts, sample prompts).
- A short eval checklist we can give our QA team.

Please send the plan and a suggested 3–4 week schedule. Procurement will need an initial SOW/estimate but can wait until we confirm scope.

Thanks,
Sanjay Patel
Head of AI Engineering
Brightlane Health

Subject: Re: Brightlane / Redwood — post-call summary + target success criteria

Sanjay — thanks for the clear summary. Attaching a draft POC timeline and the sample dashboard we propose (Brightlane_POC_Timeline.xlsx, redwood-poc-dashboard-sample.png). High-level plan below; happy to adjust once we have your QA prompt set.

POC objective: Validate performance, reliability, and observability for the Summarization routing pipeline.

Deliverables
- Instrumented Redwood test endpoint with request_id tracing and structured logs.
- Set of Grafana-style dashboards (hosted by us or exported JSON) covering latency, errors, throughput, token cost, cache metrics.
- Export pipeline to your S3 (compressed NDJSON) + OTLP to your metrics backend if you want (Datadog/NewRelic/Splunk).
- Evaluation checklist and a 72-hour sustained-run report at the end of the POC.

Owners (Redwood)
- Rafael Mendes — POC lead / commercial contact (coordination, timeline, acceptance)
- Marissa Cole — Observability & SLO definitions (dashboards, alerts, runbooks)
- Jordan Blake — Network & infra (VPC peering, allowlist, private endpoints)
- Laura Bennett — Integration engineer (prompt set onboarding, sample traffic generator)

Proposed timeline (4 weeks)
- Week 0 (kickoff): account onboarding, share prompt set, provide staging host/IPs, set up credentials (3 business days).
- Week 1 (instrumentation): enable request tracing, structured logs, token counters; initial dashboard skeleton.
- Week 2 (ingest & validation): stream logs to your S3, finalize dashboards, run smoke tests, fix policy/network issues.
- Week 3 (72-hour sustained run): run acceptance test traffic, collect traces and metrics, QA evaluates outputs against prompt set.
- Week 4 (wrap & report): deliver report (latency percentiles, error breakdown, cost estimate) + handover for production readiness.

Key observability specifics we will implement
- Trace IDs: propagate request_id through the service chain and include model_variant and kernel_fallback as tags.
- Sampling: default trace sample 1% for full payloads, 100% sampling of errors. We can increase sampling during the 72-hour run if you want deeper traces.
- Logs: structured JSON with fields: timestamp, request_id, user_id, model_variant, prompt_token_count, completion_token_count, cost_estimate_tokens, error_code.
- Dashboards: POC Overview, Latency by route/model, Errors by class, Token consumption & cost, Cache hit ratio.

Access checklist we need from Brightlane
- Staging host/IPs for allowlisting, a service account for S3 writes (or bucket write credentials), a CI account to run the traffic generator, and the QA prompt set (CSV).

We will be careful about PHI handling — logs will redact any free-text fields unless you instruct otherwise and we can discuss retention in the next call.

If this looks good, we can schedule the kickoff next Monday (Mar 22).

Best,
Rafael Mendes
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
rafael.mendes@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0192

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Brightlane / Redwood — observability details and quick checklist

Adding the observability checklist we’ll implement and a short runbook for incident triage. Rafael — feel free to paste into the POC doc.

POC Observability checklist (technical)
- Dashboards (minimum):
  • POC Overview: total requests, successful responses, p50/p95/p99 latency, error rate.
  • Latency by model and route (heatmap over time).
  • Token consumption & cost: tokens/request histogram, running cost estimate.
  • Errors & retries: error codes, retry counts, upstream timeouts.
  • Cache & batching: KV cache hit ratio, average batch size, queue depth.

- Tracing
  • Request flow: frontend -> Redwood edge -> inference instance -> cache -> backend.
  • Required trace tags: request_id, model_variant, user_id (hashed if needed), cache_hit (bool), fallback_reason (enum).
  • Sampling: 1% baseline, 100% on error; we'll increase to 10% during 72-hr run if requested.

- Logs & Export
  • Structured JSON logs written to your S3 in ndjson.gz (hourly rotation).
  • Fields: timestamp, request_id, service, model_variant, prompt_tokens, completion_tokens, latency_ms, error_code, shard_id.
  • Retention: default 14 days; we can extend to 90 days under contract.

- Alerts & SLOs
  • SLOs to monitor during POC: availability >= 99%, p95 latency target as above, error rate < 1.5%.
  • Alerts: sustained p95 > threshold for 5 minutes, error rate spike > 2x baseline.

- Runbook (short)
  • Step 1: Identify request_id in logs; pull full trace and correlated logs.
  • Step 2: Check model_variant and kernel_fallback tags; if fallback observed, escalate to kernel team.
  • Step 3: If queue depth sustained > X, scale policy or throttle non-critical routes.

Requests for Brightlane (action items)
- Provide S3 bucket credentials or an IAM role we can assume.
- Provide a small sample of the QA prompt set (20 prompts) to sanity-check outputs before the sustained run.
- Confirm whether any PHI will be included; if yes, we will enable redaction and set a short retention.

I’ll prepare the dashboard JSONs and a short runbook doc for your on-call. Attaching the timeline workbook Rafael referenced.

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
Customer Reliability Lead | Redwood Inference

- Compliance: our security team expects structured logs to be redacted for PHI by default. We can share a redaction spec; please include it in the onboarding checklist and confirm completion before the 72-hr run.

- Procurement: procurement@brightlane.health — please start the SOW with the estimate Rafael shared in the call (high-level estimate OK for now). We expect sign-off to take 7–10 business days. That may push final production decisions but should not block the 4-week POC.

We can confirm kickoff next Tuesday (Mar 23) instead of Mar 22 to give our security team a day to finalize the redaction spec. Rafael — please send an updated schedule taking that into account and the exact credentials format you need for S3 role/assume.
